name: Pesce all'Acqua Pazza
description: Whole sea bream or bass simmered in 'crazy water' — a broth of olive oil, cherry tomatoes, garlic, and white wine that is barely a sauce, barely a broth, and perfectly Neapolitan.

ingredients.note: Whole sea bream or sea bass (gutted, scaled, 500–700 g each)
Dried red chili flakes (or fresh peperoncino)

name: Agedashi Tofu
description: Silken tofu cubes dusted in potato starch and fried until their coating puffs into a trembling, semi-translucent shell, then set adrift in warm tentsuyu broth that seeps through the crust in real time — agedashi is the izakaya dish that teaches you the beauty of transience.

ingredients.note: Neutral frying oil; for frying (only some is absorbed)
Grated daikon, grated ginger, katsuobushi, green onion

name: Agedashi Tofu (gluten-free)
description: Silken tofu cubes dusted in potato starch and fried until their coating puffs into a trembling, semi-translucent shell, then set adrift in warm tentsuyu broth that seeps through the crust in real time — agedashi is the izakaya dish that teaches you the beauty of transience. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Neutral frying oil; for frying (only some is absorbed)
Grated daikon, grated ginger, katsuobushi, green onion

name: Akara (Black-Eyed Pea Fritters)
description: Black-eyed peas ground into a light, aerated batter — their skins removed so the paste is pure white and clean-tasting — then dropped by spoonfuls into hot oil where they puff, turn golden, and develop a crust that crackles while hiding a steaming, pillowy interior flecked with onion and chili.

ingredients.note: Dried black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and skins removed
Fresh scotch bonnet or habanero pepper, chopped
Vegetable (for deep-frying); the source also suggests a nut option; use the first one; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Al Pastor
description: Thin-sliced pork shoulder marinated in a paste of dried chilies, achiote, and pineapple — sweet, smoky, tangy, and ferociously flavourful. Traditionally carved from a trompo spit; equally spectacular shaved under a broiler.

ingredients.note: Dried guajillo chilies, stems and seeds removed
Dried ancho chili, stem and seeds removed

name: Alfajores de Maizena
description: Argentina's beloved sandwich cookie — two tender, crumbly cornstarch shortbread discs joined by dulce de leche and rolled in shredded coconut; they dissolve on the tongue in a wave of caramel and butter before you've finished chewing.

name: Alfajores de Maizena (gluten-free)
description: Argentina's beloved sandwich cookie — two tender, crumbly cornstarch shortbread discs joined by dulce de leche and rolled in shredded coconut; they dissolve on the tongue in a wave of caramel and butter before you've finished chewing. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Aloo Gobi
description: The homey Punjabi dry-sautéed curry of potato and cauliflower — both vegetables coated in turmeric and cumin and cooked until tender and speckled golden, with no sauce except the fragrant ghee they were tossed in.

ingredients.note: Waxy potatoes (Yukon Gold), cut into 2 cm cubes
Kashmiri chili powder or mild red chili powder

name: Pasta all'Amatriciana
description: The sauce of Amatrice — guanciale rendered until amber and crackling in its own fat, deglazed with white wine, San Marzano tomatoes added and reduced to a fiery, porky slick that clings to bucatini in rust-red sheets, crowned with Pecorino Romano sharp enough to cut through all that richness.

ingredients.note: Guanciale (cured pork cheek, cut into lardons or thick batons)
San Marzano tomatoes (crushed by hand from a 400 g can)
Dried red chilli flakes (or 1 small dried peperoncino, crumbled)

name: Pasta all'Amatriciana (gluten-free)
description: The sauce of Amatrice — guanciale rendered until amber and crackling in its own fat, deglazed with white wine, San Marzano tomatoes added and reduced to a fiery, porky slick that clings to bucatini in rust-red sheets, crowned with Pecorino Romano sharp enough to cut through all that richness. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free spaghetti instead of spaghetti.

ingredients.note: Guanciale (cured pork cheek, cut into lardons or thick batons)
San Marzano tomatoes (crushed by hand from a 400 g can)
Dried red chilli flakes (or 1 small dried peperoncino, crumbled)

name: Anticuchos de Corazón
description: Lima's iconic street-grilled beef heart skewers — heart slices marinated overnight in ají panca, cumin, and vinegar, then grilled fast over charcoal until charred at the edges and just-tender inside.

ingredients.note: Beef heart, trimmed of fat, membrane, and ventricle tubes, cut into 3cm cubes
Ají panca paste (or dried ají panca, soaked and blended)
Boiled Peruvian corn (choclo) or corn on the cob, cut into rounds

name: Classic Double-Crust American Apple Pie
description: The American standard — a shattering, lard-and-butter crust enclosing a cinnamon-brown sugar filling of thinly sliced apples that have released and reabsorbed their juice into a glossy, jammy interior. The top crust is latticed, burnished with egg wash and sugar, crackled and amber at the edges.

ingredients.note: Granny Smith and Honeycrisp apples (mixed), peeled, cored, sliced 5 mm
Light brown sugar + granulated sugar (mixed equal parts)

name: Classic Double-Crust American Apple Pie (gluten-free)
description: The American standard — a shattering, lard-and-butter crust enclosing a cinnamon-brown sugar filling of thinly sliced apples that have released and reabsorbed their juice into a glossy, jammy interior. The top crust is latticed, burnished with egg wash and sugar, crackled and amber at the edges. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Granny Smith and Honeycrisp apples (mixed), peeled, cored, sliced 5 mm
Light brown sugar + granulated sugar (mixed equal parts)

name: Apple Strudel
description: Viennese apfelstrudel — a tissue-thin dough stretched over a flour-dusted tablecloth until you can read a newspaper through it, filled with spiced apples and breadcrumbs, rolled into a log, and baked until the pastry shatters into translucent, butter-soaked layers.

ingredients.note: High-gluten bread flour or all-purpose flour
Tart apples (Granny Smith or Cox), peeled, thinly sliced

name: Apple Tarte Tatin
description: Apples caramelized to amber in butter and sugar, then blanketed under a crisp pastry lid and inverted — the upside-down tart that invented itself by accident in the Loire Valley.

ingredients.note: Firm apples (Golden Delicious or Braeburn), peeled, halved, cored
Puff pastry or shortcrust, rolled to 3 mm
Vanilla pod, split and seeds scraped

name: Apple Tarte Tatin (gluten-free)
description: Apples caramelized to amber in butter and sugar, then blanketed under a crisp pastry lid and inverted — the upside-down tart that invented itself by accident in the Loire Valley. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free pastry instead of puff pastry.

ingredients.note: Firm apples (Golden Delicious or Braeburn), peeled, halved, cored
instead of Puff pastry or shortcrust, rolled to 3 mm
Vanilla pod, split and seeds scraped

name: Arancini al Ragù
description: Golden, fist-sized spheres of saffron-tinted rice encasing a molten core of slow-cooked meat ragù and stretchy mozzarella — the crust shatters at the first bite, giving way to a steaming, savory interior that Palermo street vendors have perfected for centuries.

ingredients.note: Warm water or light chicken stock
Saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
Low-moisture mozzarella, cut into 1 cm cubes
Neutral frying oil (sunflower); the source also suggests a nut option; use the first one; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Arancini al Ragù (gluten-free)
description: Golden, fist-sized spheres of saffron-tinted rice encasing a molten core of slow-cooked meat ragù and stretchy mozzarella — the crust shatters at the first bite, giving way to a steaming, savory interior that Palermo street vendors have perfected for centuries. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free breadcrumbs instead of breadcrumbs.

ingredients.note: Warm water or light chicken stock
Saffron threads, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
Low-moisture mozzarella, cut into 1 cm cubes
Neutral frying oil (sunflower); the source also suggests a nut option; use the first one; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Arroz con Leche
description: A slow-cooked Spanish rice pudding where the starch from the rice thickens the milk naturally until it becomes a single, unctuous mass that ripples when the pot is stirred. Lemon zest and a cinnamon stick infuse as the rice swells, and the finished pudding is served cold, with a stripe of ground cinnamon across the top that disappears into its surface like earth into snow.

name: Arroz Rojo (Mexican Red Rice)
description: Mexico's indispensable side dish — long-grain rice toasted in oil until each grain turns a pale blond, then simmered in a blended tomato, garlic and onion sauce until the grains are individually coral-red, fluffy and separate, perfumed with cumin.

ingredients.note: Chicken or vegetable broth; made up to 600 ml with boiling water

name: Arroz Verde
description: Mexican green rice — long-grain rice toasted in oil until each grain turns translucent and nutty, then cooked in a blended purée of poblano pepper, jalapeño, cilantro, garlic, and onion until every grain is stained a vivid, verdant green and perfumed throughout with roasted chile.

ingredients.note: Chicken or vegetable stock; made up to 500 ml with boiling water

name: Baba Ghanoush
description: Char-roasted eggplant scooped from its skin and beaten with tahini, lemon, and garlic into a smoky, silken dip that carries the ghost of fire in every bite.

name: Baja Fish Tacos
description: Beer-battered white fish fried to a shatteringly crisp golden shell, tucked in warm corn tortillas with shredded cabbage, crema, and a squirt of lime — the taco that put Ensenada on the map.

ingredients.note: All-purpose flour and cornstarch, equal parts combined
Mexican lager beer (Modelo Especial or Pacifico), cold
Cayenne pepper and garlic powder, equal parts
Neutral oil for deep-frying (vegetable or canola); for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Baja Fish Tacos (gluten-free)
description: Gluten-free beer-battered white fish fried to a shatteringly crisp golden shell, tucked in warm corn tortillas with shredded cabbage, crema, and a squirt of lime — the taco that put Ensenada on the map. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, gluten-free beer instead of beer or ale.

ingredients.note: instead of All-purpose flour and cornstarch, equal parts combined
instead of Mexican lager beer (Modelo Especial or Pacifico), cold
Cayenne pepper and garlic powder, equal parts
Neutral oil for deep-frying (vegetable or canola); for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Baked Feta with Greens and Beans
description: A slab of feta baked until soft and golden-edged in a bubbling dish of garlicky white beans, jammy cherry tomatoes, and wilted kale. Salty, creamy, and made for mopping with torn gluten-free bread.

ingredients.note: Cannellini beans, cooked and drained (about 2 cans)
Vegetable stock; made up to 100 ml with boiling water
Lacinato kale, stems removed, leaves torn

name: Banana Oat Snack Cake
description: A moist, lightly spiced square cake made with very ripe bananas and rolled oats, with a hearty, chewy crumb, a toasty pumpkin seed top, and a deep caramel-banana sweetness that suits breakfast as well as dessert.

name: Banana Oat Snack Cake (gluten- & nut-free)
description: A moist, lightly spiced square cake made with very ripe bananas and rolled oats, with a hearty, chewy crumb, a toasty toasted seed top, and a deep caramel-banana sweetness that suits breakfast as well as dessert. This gluten- & nut-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, gluten-free oats instead of porridge oats.

name: Bánh Mì Caramelized Pork
description: Thin-sliced pork belly lacquered in fish-sauce caramel until the edges blacken and crisp, perfuming the kitchen with burnt sugar and soy — the kind of filling that makes a humble gluten-free bread taste like a destination.

ingredients.note: Pork belly or pork shoulder, thinly sliced (5mm)

name: Bánh Xèo Batter
description: The thin, golden, turmeric-tinted rice-flour crepe batter of Southern Vietnam — poured sizzling-hot into a very hot pan with coconut milk to make the wide, crispy-edged, shrimp-and-pork-stuffed pancake whose name means 'sizzling cake.'

ingredients.note: Neutral oil, for frying each crepe

name: Basque Burnt Cheesecake
description: A cream-cheese custard baked at furious heat until the top scorches to a deep mahogany — caramelized, almost bitter — while the center stays barely set, trembling like cold flan at room temperature.

name: Basque Burnt Cheesecake (gluten-free)
description: A cream-cheese custard baked at furious heat until the top scorches to a deep mahogany — caramelized, almost bitter — while the center stays barely set, trembling like cold flan at room temperature. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: BBQ Pulled Pork
description: A pork shoulder rubbed in brown sugar and smoked paprika, smoked low and slow until collagen surrenders into silk and the bark turns black-mahogany — pulled apart with two forks into shaggy, smoke-perfumed strands that need nothing more than a gluten-free bun and maybe some slaw.

name: Beef & Barley Stew
description: Deeply browned chuck braised slowly with mushrooms, carrots, and thyme until it yields to a spoon, the dark gravy thickened by plump, chewy pearl barley.

ingredients.note: Beef chuck, trimmed and cut into 4 cm cubes
Beef stock, low-sodium; made up to 2000 ml with boiling water

name: Beef & Brown rice Stew (gluten-free)
description: Deeply browned chuck braised slowly with mushrooms, carrots, and thyme until it yields to a spoon, the dark gravy thickened by plump, chewy brown rice. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of worcestershire sauce, brown rice instead of pearl barley.

ingredients.note: Beef chuck, trimmed and cut into 4 cm cubes
Beef stock, low-sodium; made up to 2000 ml with boiling water

name: Beef Bourguignon
description: Burgundy's great Sunday braise — beef stewed slowly in a whole bottle of red until the meat surrenders to the fork and the wine, deepened by lardons and a forest of mushrooms, reduces to a glossy, mahogany sauce that clings to every spoon.

ingredients.note: Beef chuck (cut into 5 cm cubes, patted bone-dry)
Young red Burgundy (Pinot Noir, full bottle)
Beef or veal stock (warm); made up to 150 ml with boiling water

name: Beef Bourguignon (gluten-free)
description: Burgundy's great Sunday braise — beef stewed slowly in a whole bottle of red until the meat surrenders to the fork and the wine, deepened by lardons and a forest of mushrooms, reduces to a glossy, mahogany sauce that clings to every spoon. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Beef chuck (cut into 5 cm cubes, patted bone-dry)
Young red Burgundy (Pinot Noir, full bottle)
Beef or veal stock (warm); made up to 150 ml with boiling water

name: Korean Beef Bulgogi
description: Thinly sliced beef marinated in a pear-and-soy elixir, grilled or pan-seared in seconds — sweet, savory, caramelized at the edges and irresistibly tender.

ingredients.note: Beef ribeye or sirloin, partially frozen for slicing
Scallions, thinly sliced (whites for marinade, greens for garnish)

name: Korean Beef Bulgogi (gluten-free)
description: Thinly sliced beef marinated in a pear-and-soy elixir, grilled or pan-seared in seconds — sweet, savory, caramelized at the edges and irresistibly tender. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Beef ribeye or sirloin, partially frozen for slicing
Scallions, thinly sliced (whites for marinade, greens for garnish)

name: Hungarian Beef Goulash
description: Paprika-red and deeply fragrant, this stew builds its soul in the fat that blooms the spice — the beef yields hour by hour into something that coats a wooden spoon and stains it permanently orange.

ingredients.note: Beef stock or water; made up to 400 ml with boiling water

name: Rendang Daging
description: Beef simmered for hours in coconut milk with galangal, lemongrass, and a fiery spice paste until all the liquid evaporates and the meat fries in its own released fat, turning dark, chewy, and explosively aromatic.

ingredients.note: Beef chuck or beef short rib (cut into 5 cm chunks)
Dried red chilies (soaked and seeded) or fresh long red chili
Kerisik (toasted shredded coconut, ground to paste)

name: Rendang Daging (nut-free)
description: Beef simmered for hours in coconut milk with galangal, lemongrass, and a fiery spice paste until all the liquid evaporates and the meat fries in its own released fat, turning dark, chewy, and explosively aromatic. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of candlenuts.

ingredients.note: Beef chuck or beef short rib (cut into 5 cm chunks)
Dried red chilies (soaked and seeded) or fresh long red chili
instead of Candlenuts (kemiri) or macadamia nuts
instead of Kerisik (toasted shredded coconut, ground to paste)

name: Steak Tartare
description: Hand-cut beef fillet mixed tableside with egg yolk, Dijon, capers, shallot, and Worcestershire — a classic that demands quality beef, confident seasoning, and no cooking at all.

ingredients.note: Beef fillet (center-cut, fully trimmed of sinew and silver skin)
Non-pareil capers, drained and roughly chopped

name: Steak Tartare (gluten-free)
description: Hand-cut beef fillet mixed tableside with egg yolk, Dijon, capers, shallot, and Gluten-free Worcestershire sauce — a classic that demands quality beef, confident seasoning, and no cooking at all. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of worcestershire sauce.

ingredients.note: Beef fillet (center-cut, fully trimmed of sinew and silver skin)
Non-pareil capers, drained and roughly chopped

name: Beef Wellington
description: The grand British centrepiece — a whole fillet of beef seared hard, painted with mustard, blanketed in a dry mushroom duxelles and a layer of prosciutto, then wrapped in golden puff pastry and roasted until the crust shatters over a rosy, blushing-pink core.

ingredients.note: Centre-cut beef fillet (tied, trimmed, room temperature)
Flaky sea salt & cracked black pepper

name: Beer-Batter Fish
description: Thick fillets of cod or haddock in a batter so light and shatteringly crisp it almost seems audible on the way to your mouth — pale gold and blistered, cracking open to reveal snow-white, steamed fish within. The beer is not decorative: its carbonation creates ten thousand tiny fissures that make the crust airy rather than leaden.

ingredients.note: Thick cod or haddock fillets, skin removed
Ice-cold pale ale or lager beer
Sunflower or vegetable oil, for deep frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Gluten-free beer-Batter Fish (gluten-free)
description: Thick fillets of cod or haddock in a batter so light and shatteringly crisp it almost seems audible on the way to your mouth — pale gold and blistered, cracking open to reveal snow-white, steamed fish within. The gluten-free beer is not decorative: its carbonation creates ten thousand tiny fissures that make the crust airy rather than leaden. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, gluten-free beer instead of beer or ale.

ingredients.note: Thick cod or haddock fillets, skin removed
instead of Ice-cold pale ale or lager beer
Sunflower or vegetable oil, for deep frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Onions
description: Chicken thighs braised in brown ale over a heap of slow-cooked, deeply golden onions, the sauce malty and faintly bitter, sharpened at the end with mustard and a splash of vinegar.

ingredients.note: Yellow onions, halved and thinly sliced
Brown ale or dark amber beer (not very hoppy)
Chicken stock, low-sodium; made up to 250 ml with boiling water

name: Gluten-free beer-Braised Chicken with Onions (gluten-free)
description: Chicken thighs braised in gluten-free beer over a heap of slow-cooked, deeply golden onions, the sauce malty and faintly bitter, sharpened at the end with mustard and a splash of vinegar. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, gluten-free beer instead of beer or ale.

ingredients.note: Yellow onions, halved and thinly sliced
instead of Brown ale or dark amber beer (not very hoppy)
Chicken stock, low-sodium; made up to 250 ml with boiling water

name: Ukrainian Beet Borscht
description: Ukraine's crimson national soup — beetroot, cabbage, potatoes, and tomatoes built into a vivid, deeply flavored broth that holds both sweetness and acid in tension. Finished at the table with a snow-white dollop of sour cream and a shower of fresh dill, it is the most complete bowl in Eastern European cooking.

ingredients.note: Raw beets, peeled and coarsely grated
Carrot, peeled and grated or julienned
Vegetable stock (or light beef/chicken stock); made up to 1500 ml with boiling water

name: New Orleans Beignets
description: Pillowy squares of yeasted fried dough that puff and hollow in hot oil, their thin crust shatteringly fragile under a snowstorm of powdered sugar that coats your lips and dusts your shirt — the essential Café du Monde experience.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil for frying (vegetable); for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Berbere-Braised Lamb Shoulder
description: Bone-in lamb shoulder painted in berbere's fiery, deeply aromatic spice blend, seared in niter kibbeh until ruddy-dark, then braised for hours with sweated onions until the meat falls from the bone in tender, spice-saturated shreds.

ingredients.note: Bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into large pieces
Niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced butter) or ghee
Lamb or beef stock; made up to 400 ml with boiling water
Tej (Ethiopian honey wine) or dry white wine

name: Dolsot Bibimbap
description: Steamed short-grain rice loaded with individually seasoned vegetables, a soft egg yolk, and a bold red gochujang paste — served in a screaming-hot stone bowl that crisps the rice to a golden crust.

ingredients.note: Sesame oil + butter (for dolsot bowl coating)

name: Dolsot Bibimbap (gluten-free)
description: Steamed short-grain rice loaded with individually seasoned vegetables, a soft egg yolk, and a bold red gochujang paste — served in a screaming-hot stone bowl that crisps the rice to a golden crust. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free gochujang instead of gochujang, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Sesame oil + butter (for dolsot bowl coating)

name: Birria de Res
description: Beef braised in a complex chili consommé until yielding and shreddable — the Jalisco braise that became a taco trend, served with its scarlet dipping broth.

ingredients.note: Whole cumin, dried oregano, cloves, black peppercorns — toasted and ground
Beef broth or water; made up to 400 ml with boiling water

name: Birria Tacos (Tacos de Birria)
description: Beef short ribs braised low and slow in a smoke-dark consommé of guajillo, ancho, and árbol chiles — the broth so richly gelatinous it fries to a lacquer when the corn tortilla hits the pan. Each taco is a double-dip affair: dunk the corn tortilla in the consommé, load it with shredded beef and Oaxacan cheese, then sear it until the outside blisters and the cheese melts into the meat.

name: Lamb Biryani
description: Fragrant aged basmati layered with spice-braised lamb and sealed under a tight dough crust — the dum method traps an aromatic cloud inside the pot so every grain of rice cooks in the breath of cardamom, mace and saffron rising from below. The crust is cracked open at the table in a billow of steam.

ingredients.note: Bone-in lamb shoulder, cut into 6 cm pieces
Aged basmati rice, soaked 30 min, drained
Onions, thinly sliced (for birista — fried crispy onion)
Saffron threads, steeped in 4 tbsp warm milk for 20 min

name: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani
description: Layers of saffron-stained basmati and yogurt-marinated chicken sealed under a dough-crimped lid, slow-cooked on a tawa so the steam trapped within perfumes every grain from the inside out. When the seal breaks at the table, a cloud of rose water, mace, and charred meat rises and fills the room.

ingredients.note: Biryani masala (ground: coriander, cumin, cardamom, clove, black pepper, cinnamon, mace)
Aged basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 30 min
Whole spices: bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon stick, star anise
Saffron strands steeped in 3 tbsp warm milk

name: Cuban Black Bean Soup
description: Dense, midnight-black bean soup perfumed with cumin, oregano, and a sofrito of onion, pepper, and garlic — finished with a splash of vinegar that makes the whole pot sing, served over white rice with a cool spoonful of sour cream.

name: Black Bean Tostadas with Avocado Slaw
description: Oven-crisped corn tortillas that crackle under a thick smear of cumin-scented mashed black beans, topped with a cool, creamy avocado-lime slaw and salty crumbles of cotija. Crunch, cream, and tang in every bite.

ingredients.note: Vegetable stock; made up to 100 ml with boiling water

name: Black Pepper Beef and Snap Pea Stir-Fry
description: Thin slices of flank steak seared in a smoking-hot pan and tossed with crisp snap peas and onion in a savory oyster-soy glaze loaded with coarsely cracked black pepper that tingles more than it burns.

ingredients.note: Flank steak, sliced 5 mm thick against the grain
Neutral oil with a high smoke point
Yellow onion, cut into 2 cm wedges and separated

name: Black Pepper Beef and Snap Pea Stir-Fry (gluten-free)
description: Thin slices of flank steak seared in a smoking-hot pan and tossed with crisp snap peas and onion in a savory oyster-soy glaze loaded with coarsely cracked black pepper that tingles more than it burns. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce, dry sherry instead of shaoxing rice wine, oyster sauce (gluten-free) instead of oyster sauce.

ingredients.note: Flank steak, sliced 5 mm thick against the grain
Neutral oil with a high smoke point
Yellow onion, cut into 2 cm wedges and separated

name: Black Sesame Pudding
description: A jet-black, satiny pudding built on toasted sesame paste — roasted until nutty and almost smoky, blended with coconut milk and set with agar into trembling obsidian slabs that unmold cleanly and melt on the tongue.

ingredients.note: Rock sugar, crushed, or caster sugar

name: Blackened Catfish
description: Catfish fillets blanketed in a Cajun spice rub, cooked in a screaming-hot cast-iron pan until the exterior chars to near-black and the interior stays moist — intensely smoky and spiced.

ingredients.note: Catfish fillets (skin-off, 180–220 g each, even thickness)

name: Medieval Blancmange
description: A dish from the great household cookbooks of the late Middle Ages — finely shredded chicken simmered until it falls into threads, then bound with rice and sweet almond milk into a pale, fragrant pottage. Neither quite savoury nor quite a pudding, it sits at the medieval table between the two, gently sweetened with sugar and crowned with fried almonds. The 'white food' that gives it its name was a mark of refinement, served to the sick and the noble alike.

ingredients.note: Chicken (whole capon or breasts, on the bone)
White rice (short-grain, ground to a coarse meal)
Chicken cooking broth (the poaching liquor, strained); made up to 150 ml with boiling water
Rosewater (a few drops, optional period perfume)
Whole almonds, blanched and fried in a little fat

name: Blueberry Lemon Muffins
description: Tall, tender muffins crowned with a crunchy sugar top, their soft sour-cream crumb bursting with jammy blueberries and brightened with fresh lemon zest.

name: Blueberry Lemon Muffins (gluten-free)
description: Tall, tender muffins crowned with a crunchy sugar top, their soft sour-cream crumb bursting with jammy blueberries and brightened with fresh lemon zest. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Bò Lúc Lắc (Shaking Beef)
description: Saigon's beloved stir-fry of tender beef cubes marinated in oyster sauce and garlic, seared on a screaming-hot wok until caramelized and served over watercress and sliced tomato with a lime-salt-pepper dipping sauce.

ingredients.note: Beef sirloin or tenderloin, cut into 3 cm cubes
Freshly cracked black pepper, for dipping sauce
Yellow onion, cut into 2 cm wedges

name: Bò Lúc Lắc (Shaking Beef) (gluten-free)
description: Saigon's beloved stir-fry of tender beef cubes marinated in gluten-free oyster sauce and garlic, seared on a screaming-hot wok until caramelized and served over watercress and sliced tomato with a lime-salt-pepper dipping sauce. This gluten-free version uses oyster sauce (gluten-free) instead of oyster sauce, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Beef sirloin or tenderloin, cut into 3 cm cubes
Freshly cracked black pepper, for dipping sauce
Yellow onion, cut into 2 cm wedges

name: Bok Choy in Oyster Sauce
description: Baby bok choy blanched to brilliant jade green, arranged cut-side up, and lacquered with a glossy, garlicky oyster sauce that pools in every crevice. One of the great fast Cantonese side dishes — its success entirely a matter of not overcooking the greens by a single second.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil (sunflower, rice bran, or grapeseed)

name: Bok Choy in Gluten-free oyster sauce (gluten-free)
description: Baby bok choy blanched to brilliant jade green, arranged cut-side up, and lacquered with a glossy, garlicky gluten-free oyster sauce that pools in every crevice. One of the great fast Cantonese side dishes — its success entirely a matter of not overcooking the greens by a single second. This gluten-free version uses oyster sauce (gluten-free) instead of oyster sauce, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce, dry sherry instead of shaoxing rice wine.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil (sunflower, rice bran, or grapeseed)

name: Baby Bok Choy with Garlic Oyster Sauce
description: Baby bok choy plunged into boiling salted water for ninety seconds emerges a shade of green so vivid it looks painted, still slightly firm at the stem and silky-tender at the leaf, arranged in a fan and blanketed with a glossy, golden garlic-and-oyster-sauce pan drizzle that smells of the sea and roasted allium. A dish that takes less than ten minutes from stove to table and asks nothing of you except timing and heat.

ingredients.note: Hot water or light stock; made up to 50 ml with boiling water

name: Baby Bok Choy with Garlic Gluten-free oyster sauce (gluten-free)
description: Baby bok choy plunged into boiling salted water for ninety seconds emerges a shade of green so vivid it looks painted, still slightly firm at the stem and silky-tender at the leaf, arranged in a fan and blanketed with a glossy, golden garlic-and-oyster-sauce pan drizzle that smells of the sea and roasted allium. A dish that takes less than ten minutes from stove to table and asks nothing of you except timing and heat. This gluten-free version uses oyster sauce (gluten-free) instead of oyster sauce, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

ingredients.note: Hot water or light stock; made up to 50 ml with boiling water

name: Ukrainian Borscht
description: Ukraine's emblematic ruby-red beet soup — roasted beets braised with cabbage, potato, and carrot in a tangy tomato broth, finished with a swirl of smetana and a shower of fresh dill, the color a deep, glorious crimson.

ingredients.note: Green or white cabbage, finely shredded
Waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
Whole peeled tomatoes (canned) or 3 fresh ripe tomatoes, chopped
Beef or vegetable stock; made up to 1800 ml with boiling water
Apple cider vinegar or red wine vinegar
Fine sea salt and black pepper
Smetana or sour cream, for serving

name: Braised Chicken with Green Olives & Lemon
description: Crisp-skinned chicken thighs settle into a golden, garlicky braise of fennel, onion, white wine, briny green olives, and soft slices of lemon that turn jammy and gently bitter in the oven.

ingredients.note: Fennel bulb, cored and cut into thin wedges
Chicken stock, low-sodium; made up to 400 ml with boiling water
Lemon, scrubbed, half thinly sliced and seeded, half juiced

name: Braised Red Cabbage (Rotkohl)
description: Germany's jewel-toned braised red cabbage — shredded rotkohl slow-braised with apple, vinegar, clove, and a touch of sugar until the cabbage collapses to a silky tangle of sweet-sour, spiced ribbons that deepens to a glossy garnet in the pot.

ingredients.note: Tart cooking apple, peeled and grated
Goose fat, duck fat, or neutral vegetable oil

name: Red Wine Braised Short Ribs
description: Bone-in beef short ribs seared to a deeply caramelized crust, then submerged in red wine and aromatics and braised low and slow for four hours until the collagen has melted into a glossy, trembling sauce that coats the fork in dark ribbons.

ingredients.note: Beef stock; made up to 500 ml with boiling water
Fine sea salt and black pepper

name: Wine-Braised Beef Short Ribs
description: Bone-in beef short ribs seared to a mahogany crust, then submerged in a full bottle of red wine and left to surrender slowly in a low oven until the collagen dissolves into silken richness and the meat slides from the bone at the touch of a spoon.

ingredients.note: Beef or veal stock; made up to 500 ml with boiling water

name: Brigadeiro
description: Brazil's beloved chocolate confection: sweetened condensed milk cooked with butter and cocoa powder until it pulls away from the pan into a glossy, fudge-like mass, then cooled, rolled into spheres, and coated in chocolate sprinkles.

name: Brigadeiros
description: Brazil's beloved chocolate truffles — just three ingredients cooked to a fudge that rolls into glossy balls and coats in chocolate sprinkles; the inevitable centerpiece of every Brazilian birthday table.

ingredients.note: Unsweetened cocoa powder (or 70% dark chocolate, finely grated)

name: Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Chewy, caramel-edged cookies built on butter cooked until it smells like toasted hazelnuts, packed with puddles of chopped dark chocolate and finished with a pinch of flaky salt.

ingredients.note: Egg yolk, from a large egg

name: Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies (gluten-free)
description: Chewy, caramel-edged cookies built on butter cooked until it smells like toasted hazelnuts, packed with puddles of chopped dark chocolate and finished with a pinch of flaky salt. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Egg yolk, from a large egg

name: Brussels Sprouts with Pancetta
description: Halved Brussels sprouts roasted face-down at high heat until the cut sides caramelize to bronze and the outer leaves char to crisp, crumpled edges — then tossed with crispy pancetta, toasted walnuts, lemon zest, and grated pecorino. Bitter and sweet, fatty and bright, all in one bowl.

ingredients.note: Pecorino Romano or Parmesan, finely grated
Flaky salt and coarse black pepper

name: Brussels Sprouts with Pancetta (nut-free)
description: Halved Brussels sprouts roasted face-down at high heat until the cut sides caramelize to bronze and the outer leaves char to crisp, crumpled edges — then tossed with crispy pancetta, pumpkin seeds, lemon zest, and grated pecorino. Bitter and sweet, fatty and bright, all in one bowl. This nut-free version uses pumpkin seeds instead of walnuts.

ingredients.note: Pecorino Romano or Parmesan, finely grated
Flaky salt and coarse black pepper

name: Butter-Poached Lobster (Beurre Monté)
description: Lobster tail and claw meat submerged in a shimmering, barely-trembling emulsion of pure butter, held at a temperature too low to toughen the proteins — emerging opaque-white, impossibly tender, tasting of the sea filtered through cream. This is not boiled lobster with butter on the side; this is lobster becoming butter.

name: Fluffy Buttermilk Diner Pancakes
description: The definitive American diner pancake — thick, cloud-soft, with a faint tang from real buttermilk and a caramel-gold crust on both faces. The batter is lumpy on purpose, the griddle is seasoned, and the butter browned. Everything else is just syrup.

name: Fluffy Buttermilk Diner Pancakes (gluten-free)
description: The definitive American diner pancake — thick, cloud-soft, with a faint tang from real buttermilk and a caramel-gold crust on both faces. The batter is lumpy on purpose, the griddle is seasoned, and the butter browned. Everything else is just syrup. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Butternut Squash Pasta with Brown Butter and Sage
description: Rigatoni coated in a silky sauce of roasted butternut squash blended with pasta water, tossed with nutty brown butter, crisp fried sage, and caramelized squash cubes. Sweet, savory, and autumn-warm, with toasted walnuts for crunch.

ingredients.note: Rigatoni or other short, ridged pasta

name: Butternut Squash Pasta with Brown Butter and Sage (gluten- & nut-free)
description: Rigatoni coated in a silky sauce of roasted butternut squash blended with pasta water, tossed with nutty brown butter, crisp fried sage, and caramelized squash cubes. Sweet, savory, and autumn-warm, with pumpkin seeds for crunch. This gluten- & nut-free version uses gluten-free pasta shapes instead of dried pasta, pumpkin seeds instead of walnuts.

ingredients.note: instead of Rigatoni or other short, ridged pasta

name: Butternut Squash Veloute
description: A silken, autumn-gold soup of roasted butternut squash blended with a lightly spiced vegetable stock into a velvet puree, finished with cream and a thread of brown butter — rich and sweet but balanced by a whisper of nutmeg and white pepper.

ingredients.note: Vegetable stock, hot; made up to 800 ml with boiling water
Creme fraiche or a drizzle of cream

name: Cá Kho Tộ (Caramelized Braised Fish)
description: Mekong Delta's clay-pot braised catfish — fish steaks simmered in a deeply reduced caramel of coconut water, fish sauce, and sugar until the sauce turns glossy and amber, the fish infused with a complex bittersweet savour.

ingredients.note: Catfish steaks, bone-in, 3 cm thick (cá tra or swai)
Young green coconut water (nước dừa tươi)
Spring onion greens, sliced into 3 cm pieces

name: Cacio e Pepe
description: Three ingredients — pasta, Pecorino, black pepper — governed by a principle so precise it reads more like physics than cooking: starchy water, friction, and temperature held in balance to spin a sauce that coats each strand in a seamless, peppery silk.

ingredients.note: Pasta cooking water, starchy and salted
Extra-virgin olive oil (optional, for the pan)

name: Cacio e Pepe (gluten-free)
description: Three ingredients — pasta, Pecorino, black pepper — governed by a principle so precise it reads more like physics than cooking: starchy water, friction, and temperature held in balance to spin a sauce that coats each strand in a seamless, peppery silk. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free spaghetti instead of spaghetti, gluten-free pasta shapes instead of dried pasta.

ingredients.note: instead of Tonnarelli, spaghetti, or rigatoni
Pasta cooking water, starchy and salted
Extra-virgin olive oil (optional, for the pan)

name: Caesar Salad
description: Tijuana by way of Hollywood — crisp inner romaine tossed at the table in a garlic-anchovy-egg emulsion that clings to every leaf, the whole thing tangled with shards of aged parmesan and croutons crackling with olive oil and garlic.

name: Caesar Salad (gluten-free)
description: Tijuana by way of Hollywood — crisp inner romaine tossed at the table in a garlic-anchovy-egg emulsion that clings to every leaf, the whole thing tangled with shards of aged parmesan and gluten-free croutons crackling with olive oil and garlic. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of worcestershire sauce, gluten-free bread instead of crusty white bread.

ingredients.note: instead of Day-old rustic bread, cubed (for croutons)

name: Calamari Fritti
description: Crisp, airy fried squid rings and tentacles dusted in seasoned semolina and dropped in hot oil until shattering gold — served immediately with lemon wedges, because the thirty-second window between perfect and limp is real and unforgiving.

ingredients.note: Fine semolina (or half 00 flour, half semolina)
the source also suggests a nut option; use the first one; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Camarones al Mojo de Ajo
description: Jumbo shrimp blistered in an obscene quantity of slowly toasted garlic, butter, lime, and a touch of guajillo — the kind of dish you mop the plate for.

ingredients.note: Jumbo shrimp, head-on if possible (deveined, shells on or off)
Neutral oil or light olive oil
Guajillo chili (dried, stemmed and seeded, cut into strips or crumbled)
Fresh cilantro and lime wedges (for serving)

name: Canelé de Bordeaux
description: A vanilla-and-rum custard batter rested 48 hours, poured into beeswax-coated copper moulds, and baked at two temperatures — producing a nearly burnt, mahogany shell that shatters to reveal a moist, custardy interior.

name: Canelé de Bordeaux (gluten-free)
description: A vanilla-and-rum custard batter rested 48 hours, poured into beeswax-coated copper moulds, and baked at two temperatures — producing a nearly burnt, mahogany shell that shatters to reveal a moist, custardy interior. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Cannoli Cream
description: Freshly strained ricotta whipped with powdered sugar, orange zest, and chocolate chips — the soul of Sicily in a bowl, ethereally light when the ricotta is properly drained, with a clean dairy sweetness that the orange cuts through like a knife.

name: Cannoli Cream (nut-free)
description: Freshly strained ricotta whipped with powdered sugar, orange zest, and chocolate chips — the soul of Sicily in a bowl, ethereally light when the ricotta is properly drained, with a clean dairy sweetness that the orange cuts through like a knife. This nut-free version uses pumpkin seeds instead of pistachios.
